live: a button runs the three cells again at the size picked (the largest by default, the middle size on a narrow screen) on a separate in-memory database in your browser, apart from the page's database, and shows each cell's result and engine time; a second button runs the count and the walk again from a node you name; it shows how much memory that database's engine holds; Free closes it and returns the memory.
text:
The scale demo runs cells `tree-build`, `tree-count` and `tree-walk` again with `n` set to 1,000, 10,000 or 100,000, on an in-memory database of its own in the browser tab: a second copy of the engine, so the page's database never holds the large graph. `tree-build` creates the tree, `tree-count` counts its nodes and relationships, and `tree-walk` follows every chain of relationships down from one node. It shows each cell's first row and the time the engine took, beside the cell's recording. It offers 100,000 nodes first on a wide screen and 10,000 on a narrow one, says how much memory the second engine holds, and closes that engine on Free, on the engine bar's Reset, and when the page is left.
